خَيْطَفٌ , (K,) or ↓ خَطِيفٌ , (S, [so in my copies,]) (assumed tropical:) A quick, or swift, camel; (S, K, TA;) as though he strained, or stretched, his neck, in going along: (S: [see 8:]) and the former, (assumed tropical:) a camel of the [excellent and swift] kind called مَهَارِىّ: pl. خَيَاطِفُ. (TA.) ―
-b2- خَيْطَفٌ, (TA,) or ↓ خَطَفَى , (JK,) [as meaning (assumed tropical:) Quick,] is also applied to [the pace termed] عَنَقٌ; (JK, TA;) and so ↓ خَيْطَفَى . (JK.) ―
-b3- See also خَطَفَى.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
